question: Does tax-loss harvesting create real economic value, or is it just deferring the tax bill (plus wash-sale risk and transaction cost) for nothing?
summary: Deferral alone has real but modest time-value benefit; the actual engine of value is short-term/long-term rate arbitrage (harvest at 37%, eventually pay at 20%), amplified by step-up-at-death or charitable giving converting deferral into permanent avoidance. Wash-sale-forced substitution is the real friction cost. Matches Kitces/robo-advisor corpus closely; missed the $3,000/year ordinary-income offset mechanic and underweighted that benefit size is capped by deferral time-value, not the full rate spread.
